messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 1752000456 High 5xx rate from eu-west-1 (multiple AZs). >50% error rate on /api/v1/search for tenancy=redwood-customer-prod :rotating_light:

maria: paging @kevin_oncall and @ashwin. Looks like network errors across services in eu-west-1. Observability shows spikes aligned with a terraform apply ~1751999800.

kevin_oncall: on it. grabbing logs + looking at route tables. Can someone post the TF change? @deploy-bot any recent applies?

deploy-bot: @maria @kevin_oncall terraform apply completed by chris at 1751999798 for workspace=prod-eu-west-1. Plan summary: 2 changes (1 update, 1 replace).

maria: uploading snippet of the change:

chris: pasted the relevant change (copied from PR):
```
resource "aws_route_table_association" "web_subnet_a" {
  subnet_id      = "subnet-0a1b2c3d"
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.private_rt.id # was previously assoc with private_rt-eu-a
}
```

ashwin: that looks suspicious. I see private_rt was swapped to a public-facing RT in one AZ during the apply which removed the NAT gateway route in that AZ. egress from subnets in eu-west-1a is now going directly to an IGW and losing return path to some managed endpoints (asymmetric routing).

sofia_support: customers in EU reporting failures for background syncs and search indexing. Affected: ~8% of accounts (all in eu-west region).

kevin_oncall: confirming: CloudWatch shows 502/504 spikes from services pinned to eu-west-1a. Route table lookup:
```
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c3d
```
Result: associated route table has default route 0.0.0.0/0 -> igw-0abcd, no nat target. NAT gateway nat-0ef12 still exists in eu-west-1a but not referenced.

maria: severity set to P1, paging pager duty escalation to infra-sre. @jess_product can you confirm customer-facing comms?

jess_product: draft status page: "We are investigating elevated error rates for customers in eu-west-1. Some background jobs and API requests may fail intermittently. Engineers are working on mitigation." Will update at +30m or on a significant milestone.

ashwin: immediate mitigation options: 
- Re-associate subnet with correct private route table (fast), OR
- Recreate route to nat-0ef12 if safer, OR
- Provision temporary NAT instance and modify RT to point to it (avoid TF until safe).

kevin_oncall: prefer minimal-change manual fix to restore traffic quickly and then revert TF state. I'll attempt manual route table association to restore NAT path. Doing `aws ec2 replace-route-table-association` now.

kevin_oncall: (2m later) replace-route-table-association returned association-id-rtbassoc-12345. Doing test curl to external healthcheck endpoint from app host in subnet.

kevin_oncall: curl test passed, dns resolution ok, hitting external endpoint over NAT. Observability shows error rates dropping in eu-west-1a.

maria: great. Can you confirm rollback plan for TF? We should avoid another unintended change.

chris: TF state currently thinks association is with the wrong RT (because apply already mutated infra). I recommend:
1) Lock TF state, create plan that re-associates to private_rt explicitly, but *do not apply* until we coordinate.
2) We should import current association into state to avoid TF drift.

ashwin: also found a stale NACL rule that denies ephemeral port egress for 1024-65535 in eu-west-1a (added by previous debug run). That would have caused asymmetric failure for some services. I just removed the deny rule manually.

sofia_support: customer-impact notes for postmortem: ~8% accounts, escalations from 3 enterprise customers, ingestion backlog ~120k messages delayed. No data loss.

jess_product: will send interim update: "Mitigation in progress; partial restoration observed in eu-west-1a. We're working on a full fix and will share timeline."

kevin_oncall: monitoring. Will keep this thread as ground truth for actions. If rates hold under 2% error, will start a controlled TF reconcile with chris.

maria: handing off to @ashwin for deeper root cause and remediation follow-ups. I'm stepping out but will join for postmortem.

ashwin: root cause summary so far (working): terraform apply accidentally swapped route_table_association for subnet-0a1b2c3d to a public RT, removing NAT egress. Secondary contributing factor: stale NACL deny rule blocking ephemeral ports prevented retries/established connections. Combined caused asymmetric routing and 5xx errors for customers pinned to the affected AZ.

chris: remediation actions assigned:
- chris: create TF plan to set association to private_rt and import current association id (ETA 25m)
- ashwin: audit all route table association changes in last 24h and NACL diffs (ETA 1h)
- kevin_oncall: validate throttling and SLOs, keep monitoring (ongoing)
- sofia_support/jess_product: customer comms updates + ticket triage (ongoing)

deploy-bot: scheduled a rollback plan id: RB-1752001123 for review (manual approval required).

maria: moving to incidents/monitoring-checklist: please capture all logs + retain at least 14d. Also create a postmortem doc and link here when ready.

sofia_support: created support tickets for the 3 enterprise customers and sent interim messages. No escalations to legal.

kevin_oncall: at +18m error rate stable ~1.8% and falling. I've left the manual association in place and will not apply TF until we import state.

ashwin: one more safety note: ensure cross-AZ ELBs still healthy — I saw one NLB target in eu-west-1b going unhealthy due to cross-region replication lag triggered by the same glitch. Rebalancing in progress.

jess_product: will schedule a customer debrief for enterprise customers in eu on Monday.

maria: closing immediate alert once error rate <1% for 10m. Keeping thread open for RCA. Thanks all for fast response :thumbsup:

kevin_oncall: final check at 1752002321: error rate steady 0.6% in eu-west; marking incident as mitigated. Will follow up with timeline and RCA in separate postmortem.
